cards.power: The Brittle-Buff. No stress-shield. Minor infections end the match.
cards.lore: The Glass Model. Homeostatic reserve so thin that small events trigger system failure.
cards.gradeReason: Name alone performs the clinical phenotype. Instantly embody it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage wrestling card. Subject: gaunt gazelle on crumbling pedestal. Mood: fragile defiance.

cards.power: The Gravity-Weakness. Melts the motor. Cannot push out of chairs or catch falls.
cards.lore: Driven by inflammaging. Type II fibers vanish; fat infiltrates.
cards.gradeReason: Muscle loss as a wasting villain — zero explanation needed at any table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medical kayfabe poster. Subject: rusting armored rhino shedding muscle mass. Mood: slow decay.

cards.power: The Narrow-Path. Too much water? Pulmonary edema. Too little? Renal failure.
cards.lore: Natural organ decline. Normal at rest, collapses under stress.
cards.gradeReason: Narrow homeostatic window as a wrestling constraint — clinically precise and immediately performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tightrope illustration. Subject: mountain goat balanced on impossibly thin wire over twin abysses. Mood: precarious equilibrium.

cards.power: The Interaction-Web. Heart treatments hurt the kidneys; cascading failures.
cards.lore: Polypharmacologic destruction. A network of interlinked malfunctions.
cards.gradeReason: Octopus comorbidity monster — every tentacle is a different diagnosis. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: kayfabe monster card. Subject: octopus with organ-themed tentacles pulling multiple wrestlers down. Mood: systemic overwhelm.

cards.power: The Chemical-Crossfire. Pills fight each other, triggering the Prescription Cascade.
cards.lore: Meds prescribed to treat side effects of other meds, ignoring root causes.
cards.gradeReason: Pill-hoarder squirrel exploding with meds — you instantly know what this character does.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaotic comedy card. Subject: frantic squirrel juggling explosively interacting pill bottles. Mood: pharmaceutical chaos.

cards.power: The Saboteur-Signal. Hidden traps triggering falls, bleeding, and confusion.
cards.lore: Altered pharmacokinetics: higher body fat extends benzo half-life.
cards.gradeReason: Blacklisted meds as a crow holding a scroll of forbidden names — instantly actionable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wanted-poster card. Subject: sinister crow clutching scroll labeled Benzos/Opioids/NSAIDs. Mood: forbidden danger.

cards.power: The Brain-Cloud. Dries the mouth, blocks the bladder, fogs the thinking.
cards.lore: Acetylcholine blockade. Inevitably causes cognitive deficits and hallucinations.
cards.gradeReason: Anticholinergic fog owl with ACB Score stat — clinically complete and immediately usable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hazy impressionist card. Subject: spectral owl dissolving into fog, blurring patient face behind. Mood: cognitive obscuration.

cards.power: The Tactical-Withdrawal. Removes unnecessary cards. Less is more.
cards.lore: Targeted cessation where risk outweighs benefit. Restores balance.
cards.gradeReason: Deprescribing hero raccoon dismantling pill towers — the antidote card every med student needs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hero action card. Subject: raccoon systematically dismantling tower of medication boxes. Mood: strategic liberation.

cards.power: The Reality-Glitch. Patients pull tubes and fail to recognize family.
cards.lore: Acute Brain Failure. The brain loses all compensation for stress.
cards.gradeReason: Chameleon delirium — shifting reality, CAM positive stat — zero ambiguity, fully performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychedelic medical card. Subject: chameleon dissolving into swirling hospital hallucination. Mood: acute reality fracture.

cards.power: The Memory-Void. Erases appointments, names, then swallowing.
cards.lore: Neurodegeneration via Beta-Amyloid and Tau. Hippocampus shrinks first.
cards.gradeReason: Elephant erasing its own memory book — the deck's most iconic card. Unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melancholic portrait card. Subject: elephant erasing pages from memory chronicle, hippocampus shrinking. Mood: inevitable loss.

cards.power: The Ghost-Show. Summons detailed room figures. Deathly allergic to antipsychotics!
cards.lore: Alpha-synuclein deposits. Wakefulness and dreaming commonly dissolve.
cards.gradeReason: Walrus hallucinating spectral figures with antipsychotic allergy warning baked in — clinical gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ghostly horror card. Subject: walrus surrounded by vivid spectral apparitions, red X through antipsychotic symbol. Mood: dream-waking dissolution.

cards.power: The Fluid-Pressure. Gait becomes broad-based and magnetic.
cards.lore: CSF outflow disorder. Without fast fixation, the Liquor Tap Test works a miracle of temporary recovery.
cards.gradeReason: Penguin in fishbowl helmet — wet/wobbly/wacky triad is the most memorable diagnostic cluster in geriatrics.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: quirky diagnostic card. Subject: penguin in glass helmet with fluid sloshing, magnetic feet shuffling. Mood: absurdly precise.

cards.power: The Midnight-Fade. Standing cuts lights in the brain; the fall is inevitable.
cards.lore: Baroreceptor dysfunction. The brain becomes a dry dock.
cards.gradeReason: Giraffe going dark on standing — BP drop stat and baroreceptor lore click instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dusk-lit card. Subject: giraffe neck drooping as lights dim, BP numbers fading. Mood: gravity wins at midnight.

cards.power: The Game-Over. Surgery < 24 hours, or the complication death-cycle begins.
cards.lore: Femoral neck fracture. Without fast fixation, pneumonia and thrombosis finish the job.
cards.gradeReason: Ostrich with shortened rotated leg — Game-Over framing makes the 24h window impossible to forget.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: emergency alert card. Subject: ostrich mid-fall, leg snapped, surgery clock ticking to zero. Mood: urgent deadline.

cards.power: The Mobility-Radar. Instantly spots if a wrestler is about to trip.
cards.lore: Tests strength, coordination, and balance in one fluid movement.
cards.gradeReason: Cheetah on a caution-taped course — TUG test as a mobility radar is pedagogically perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: speed-test card. Subject: cheetah navigating caution tape obstacle course, stopwatch visible. Mood: calibrated urgency.

cards.power: The Flesh-Eater. Strikes when movement stops, digging down to the bone.
cards.lore: Ischemia through pressure. Tissue dies quietly from the inside out.
cards.gradeReason: Flesh-eating turtle burrowing inward — Braden Scale stat and silent tissue death framing are surgical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: horror medical card. Subject: armored turtle burrowing into cracked earth, bone visible beneath. Mood: silent destruction.

cards.power: The Liquid-Betrayal. Unpredictable bladder leading to shame and wet nighttime falls.
cards.lore: Detrusor overactivity. Often the trigger for Nursing Home Exile.
cards.gradeReason: Basset hound urinary betrayal is vivid but detrusor lore requires med context to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melancholic comedy card. Subject: dejected basset hound mid-puddle, moonlit hospital corridor. Mood: dignity at stake.

cards.power: The Abdominal-Bake. Digestion stops, toxins rise. Can directly trigger delirium!
cards.lore: Reduced motility + low water intake + polypharmacy.
cards.gradeReason: Sloth intestine = constipation = delirium trigger. The exclamation point sells the clinical cascade.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sluggish biology card. Subject: sloth entangled in slow gut coils, blockage glowing amber. Mood: toxic standstill.

cards.power: The Wrong-Pipe-Slide. Diverts food into lungs. Direct result: aspiration pneumonia.
cards.lore: Loss of neuromuscular coordination.
cards.gradeReason: Pelican misdirecting bolus is clear but Dot diminutive reduces wrestling-archetype gravitas slightly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anatomical mishap card. Subject: pelican with food routing arrows going wrong-pipe red. Mood: silent aspiration danger.

cards.power: The Energy-Drain. Steals the power for healing. Muscle cannot be repaired.
cards.lore: Anorexia of aging. Loss of taste and poor dentition cause severe wasting.
cards.gradeReason: Wasted lioness draining life energy — the misdiagnosed-as-normal-aging lore is the teaching point every student needs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wasting portrait card. Subject: gaunt lioness with energy meter draining to empty. Mood: depletion without drama.

cards.power: The Silence-Wall. Total isolation. Those who cannot hear withdraw and demend faster.
cards.lore: Deafness is dangerous. Social isolation is the most dangerous secondary debuff.
cards.gradeReason: Bat bouncing off a brick wall is vivid but Presby requires audiological literacy to immediately land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: isolation card. Subject: bat broadcasting sonar into a brick wall of silence, alone. Mood: communicative exile.

cards.power: The Fog-Vision. Makes the world yellow/blurry, turning obstacles into deadly traps.
cards.lore: Denaturation of lens proteins. Lens replacement is the ultimate Healing Ritual.
cards.gradeReason: Lemur peering through clouded glass — fog-vision that turns obstacles into traps is poetic and precise.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hazy vision card. Subject: lemur gazing through yellowed opaque lens, sharp world visible beyond. Mood: clarity just out of reach.

cards.power: The Tunnel-Vision. Steals sight from the outside in, until only a pinprick remains.
cards.lore: Optic nerve damage. The silent thief causes zero pain until it's too late.
cards.gradeReason: Silent thief stealing peripheral vision — the tunnel shrinking to a pinprick is the perfect clinical metaphor.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir theft card. Subject: hawk stealing field of vision, leaving only a pinhole circle of sight. Mood: painless disappearance.

cards.power: The Room-Spin. Destroys orientation. Every step is a massive test of courage.
cards.lore: Multifactorial: the data from eyes, ears, and feet no longer match in the brain.
cards.gradeReason: Flamingo on a spinning record, Romberg Test stat — visceral, immediately playable, clinically complete.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dizzying vortex card. Subject: flamingo mid-spin on vinyl record, sensory signals mismatching. Mood: orientation dissolved.

cards.power: The Vital-Eroder. Steals sleep. The secret engine driving Delirium-Daze.
cards.lore: Pain in old age is totally underestimated or falsely dismissed as normal.
cards.gradeReason: Buffalo worn down by pain is evocative but Punk-zine marker type tag is unclear at first glance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grind-worn card. Subject: battered buffalo marked with NRS pain diary, sleep eroding around it. Mood: unacknowledged suffering.

cards.power: The Night-Riot. Causes nighttime wandering — or triggers dangerous benzo prescriptions.
cards.lore: Altered sleep architecture; deep sleep drops dramatically.
cards.gradeReason: Rooster causing night riots and triggering benzo prescriptions — the double danger is clinically brilliant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: night-terror card. Subject: rooster crowing at midnight in hospital ward, benzo pill falling in background. Mood: nocturnal disruption.

cards.power: The Pseudodementia. Mimics Alz-the-Eraser! They just lack the energy to remember.
cards.lore: Highly treatable. Triggered by compounding loss of partner, health, or societal role.
cards.gradeReason: The pseudodementia hook — Depression mimics Alzheimer's — is the deck's most important clinical teaching moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: shadow portrait card. Subject: bulldog in underground bunker, shadow-double resembling Alz-the-Eraser behind. Mood: treatable darkness.

cards.power: The Support-Collapse. If Sam falls, no one hears him. Home care is impossible.
cards.lore: The single strongest non-medical predictor of mortality in old age.
cards.gradeReason: Wolf alone in spotlight — the mortality stat in lore is the most chilling sentence in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: existential isolation card. Subject: single wolf under spotlight in vast empty hospital corridor. Mood: systemic abandonment.

cards.power: The Sovereign-Voice. Stops the Surgical Scrimmage when interventions become futile.
cards.lore: The ultimate document of autonomy. Defines the hard boundaries of medical intervention.
cards.gradeReason: Living Will as a golden crest card — Sovereign-Voice framing elevates patient autonomy to its rightful status.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heraldic authority card. Subject: stag bearing golden living-will crest, halting surgical team. Mood: dignified finality.

cards.power: The Comfort-Shield. Ends the fight against the inevitable, begins the fight for freedom from pain.
cards.lore: Not giving more days to life, but more life to the days.
cards.gradeReason: The lore quote is one of the most resonant sentences in all of medicine — card earns Grade 1 on that alone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gentle epic card. Subject: butterfly and bear together, comfort shield deflecting pain waves. Mood: compassionate strength.

cards.power: The Safe-Exit. The final round is fought with dignity, free from unnecessary tubes.
cards.lore: Specialisation is dying as a natural, supported part of the life process.
cards.gradeReason: Tortoise in a garden haven — Safe-Exit as a gentle positive reframe of hospice deserves wide clinical teaching use.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: peaceful sanctuary card. Subject: ancient tortoise resting in blooming garden, tubes absent. Mood: dignified completion.

cards.power: The Natural-End. Prevents ribs from being broken and shocks from being delivered at the end.
cards.lore: The clinical decision against resuscitation when medically futile.
cards.gradeReason: STOP sign badger with flatline monitor — blunt, necessary, clinically irreducible. Perfect card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: decisive authority card. Subject: badger holding red STOP sign before cardiac monitor, dignified posture. Mood: firm compassion.

cards.power: The Independence-Meter. Calculates the precise level of physical help needed daily.
cards.lore: The critical tool for planning care levels and determining if discharge is safe.
cards.gradeReason: Butler metaphor is clever but a scoring index as a character is less immediately performative than villain cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: service assessment card. Subject: formal penguin butler with checklist clipboard, rating ADL activities. Mood: precise care planning.

cards.power: The Cognition-Compass. Reveals exactly which parts of the map Alz-the-Eraser has deleted.
cards.lore: A coarse but globally standardized screening for basic cognitive and orientation deficits.
cards.gradeReason: Mapping lost cognition is vivid but MMSE needs the Alz crossref to fully activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartography card. Subject: fox plotting brain-map with missing terrain patches. Mood: standardized discovery.

cards.power: The Triage-Eye. Filters out ER patients who need complex geriatric care vs. standard care.
cards.lore: Prevents high-risk seniors from becoming revolving door patients immediately after discharge.
cards.gradeReason: Triage-Eye is strong but ISAR acronym is opaque without prior exposure.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: emergency filter card. Subject: chameleon with triage binoculars sorting ER patients at hospital gate. Mood: rapid precision.

cards.power: The Executive-Check. Failing shows total loss of frontal lobe control over multi-step tasks.
cards.lore: Tests visuospatial construction and executive cognitive function simultaneously.
cards.gradeReason: Beaver drawing a chaotic clock — Set time 11:10 stat and frontal-lobe failure framing are clinical perfection.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: executive function card. Subject: beaver frantically drawing wrong clock, numbers scattered. Mood: frontal collapse made visible.

cards.power: The Congestion-Creep. The heart is stiff, not weak. Water backs up into the lungs.
cards.lore: The stiff heart of aging. Typical after decades of hypertension and diabetes.
cards.gradeReason: Bull-in-a-cage HFpEF — stiff not weak corrects the most common misconception in one phrase.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: caged flood card. Subject: bull heart in rusted cage, water rising into lung space above. Mood: passive flooding.

cards.power: The Toxin-Builder. Standard medication doses accumulate into fatal toxins.
cards.lore: Age-related nephron loss. The entire foundation of pharmacological elimination crumbles.
cards.gradeReason: Raccoon with leaking pipes is effective but Ray as a name feels less anchored than the villain cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: toxic accumulation card. Subject: raccoon surrounded by accumulating toxic dose vials, GFR meter falling. Mood: invisible overdose building.

cards.power: The Breathless-Trap. Anchors the patient to the chair, letting Fiona-Frona-Fraility win by default.
cards.lore: Alveolar damage creates an unbreakable cycle of immobility and muscle wasting.
cards.gradeReason: Bulldog anchored to chair by breathlessness — the crossref to Frailty-Fiona is the deck's best systems loop.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: breathless entrapment card. Subject: bulldog tethered to armchair by alveolar chains, candle guttering. Mood: immobile spiral.

cards.power: The Vitality-Thief. Drains energy, fatally misdiagnosed by amateurs as just getting old.
cards.lore: Often inflammation-related, or driven by occult, slow-drip bleeding in the GI tract.
cards.gradeReason: Grey peacock draining energy — the misdiagnosed-as-normal-aging lore is the teaching point every student needs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: faded elegance card. Subject: peacock with greying feathers, energy draining to monochrome. Mood: unrecognized theft.

cards.power: The Gentle-Entry. Prevents the immediate catastrophic System Crash from overdose.
cards.lore: Pharmacodynamics in old age are unpredictable. Hit the Effect Zone without touching the Toxic Zone.
cards.gradeReason: Dosing principle as a character works but rule-cards are harder to embody than entity-cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: precision entry card. Subject: mouse entering dose pipe at 25% width, toxic zone marked red ahead. Mood: measured caution.

cards.power: The Patience-Buff. Gives the fragile system time to acclimate to new chemistry.
cards.lore: The hidden accumulation of active substances is the deadliest invisible risk.
cards.gradeReason: Tortoise titration is fitting but the accumulation danger outperforms the card's name in impact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: measured pace card. Subject: tortoise advancing carefully between dose milestone flags. Mood: invisible danger of speed.

cards.power: The Bleed-Stopper. If a wrestler falls on thinners, K prevents lethal brain bleeding.
cards.lore: Rapidly restores clotting factors II, VII, IX, and K.
cards.gradeReason: VKA reversal hero is clinically vital but the full name is a mouthful; clotting factor lore is dry.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: antidote hero card. Subject: superhero carrot (Vitamin K) plugging ruptured clotting pipeline. Mood: rapid rescue.

cards.power: The Delirium-Clearer. The ultimate weapon against Daze. Flushes toxins and restarts the brain.
cards.lore: Simple dehydration is the most frequent hidden trigger for acute cognitive failure.
cards.gradeReason: Camel IV flush clearing Delirium-Daze — simplest and most underused clinical fix, perfectly packaged.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: elixir hero card. Subject: camel pouring IV fluid waterfall through a glitching brain, clarity returning. Mood: simple miracle.

cards.power: The Stasis-Breaker. Shatters the grip of Sarcopenia-Wither and Pete-the-Pressure-Sore.
cards.lore: Lying in bed in old age is a fatal disease. Movement preserves bone and muscle.
cards.gradeReason: Goat smashing stasis chains — lying in bed is a fatal disease is the most urgent sentence a junior doctor can read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: liberation action card. Subject: goat charging through bed-rails, muscle and bone rebuilding behind. Mood: urgent movement.

cards.power: The Protein-Armor-Repair. Rapidly supplies blocks needed to reconstruct tissue.
cards.lore: Direct combat against Malnutri-Molly. Food is medicine.
cards.gradeReason: Honey badger supplement drink is fun but the card as a product-type is less embodiable than a clinical entity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: power-up card. Subject: honey badger flexing after drinking supplement bottle, tissue regenerating. Mood: protein as power.

cards.power: The Safety-Net-Constructor. Rebuilds the external environment for survival at home.
cards.lore: Medicine does not end at the hospital door. Social environment dictates survival.
cards.gradeReason: Hippo safety-net is a strong concept but Social Service as a name undersells the card's clinical importance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: community infrastructure card. Subject: hippo weaving safety net of home-care connections around patient. Mood: systemic protection.

cards.power: The Anchor-Point. Locks the patient in the here and now, fending off Delirium Demons.
cards.lore: Visual and haptic stimuli forcefully stabilize neuronal orientation.
cards.gradeReason: Orangutan surrounded by familiar objects as neurological anchor — non-pharmacological delirium intervention beautifully personified.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm sanctuary card. Subject: orangutan in familiar-object circle, delirium shadows retreating at borders. Mood: anchored presence.

cards.power: The Fall-Prevention-Move. Rewires the wrestler to avoid obstacles and deploy strength.
cards.lore: Targeted rebuilding of postural core muscles and lost proprioception.
cards.gradeReason: Kangaroo on balance board rewiring proprioception — fall prevention as active rewiring is biomechanically exact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rehabilitation card. Subject: kangaroo on balance board, postural pathways glowing rebuilt. Mood: targeted restoration.

cards.power: The Tool-Master. Equips the patient with physical hardware to hack their environment.
cards.lore: Adapting the physical world to match the patient's current abilities.
cards.gradeReason: Chimp with adaptive tools is vivid but OT as a card-character needs ADL Training stat to fully activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: adaptive engineering card. Subject: chimp fitting grab-rails, raised toilet, modified kitchen. Mood: environment hacked for function.

cards.power: The Aspiration-Guard. Physically blocks Dysphagia-Dot, ensuring food bypasses the lungs.
cards.lore: Vital mechanical rehabilitation of bulbar functions to prevent pneumonia.
cards.gradeReason: Parrot swallow trainer is charming but Logo (logopaedics) needs medical vocabulary to decode instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bulbar rehab card. Subject: parrot coaching swallow arc away from lungs, pneumonia blocked. Mood: precision rehabilitation.

cards.power: The Holistic-Harmony. Synthesizes 50 data points into one safe discharge plan.
cards.lore: Treat the whole human. Start low, go slow. Is he safe at home? Stay Ruffy!
cards.gradeReason: Doc FrizzleBob as the geriatric attending — the deck's hero card and mnemonic anchor for the entire specialty.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hero attending card. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit in white coat holding discharge plan, 50 data streams converging. Mood: mastery.

cards.power: The Trigger-Hunt.
cards.lore: 80yo confused post-hip surgery. Is the trigger Sloth-the-Slow-Gut or a UTI from Ian-the-Incontinent?
cards.gradeReason: Scenario card bridging Daze + Sloth + Ian — delirium differential as a quest is the deck's best teaching mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: midnight mystery card. Subject: gazelle darting through dark hospital maze, UTI and constipation as rival clue tokens. Mood: urgent diagnostic hunt.

cards.power: The Cascade-Breaker.
cards.lore: BP meds cause dizziness — Fall — Hip Snap. BEERS x BLACKLIST! Surgery < 24h, mobilize immediately, burn the Beers-Blacklist.
cards.gradeReason: Hip fracture cascade with Beers Blacklist crossfire — the most clinically lethal geriatric scenario, packaged perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: urgent cascade card. Subject: ostrich tumbling from Beers-poison dizziness, ortho team mobilizing. Mood: system failure halted just in time.

cards.power: The Diagnosis-Split.
cards.lore: Patient stops eating, forgets dates. Is it Alzheimer's or treatable Late-Life Depression? Deploy MMSE + GDS!
cards.gradeReason: The dementia/depression differential as a binary quest — clinically critical, emotionally resonant, table-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: diagnostic split card. Subject: lioness in shadow — Alz-the-Eraser on one side, Depression-the-Dark on other. Mood: treatable vs. terminal.

cards.power: The Chemical-Purge.
cards.lore: Renal failure + 15 meds = toxic accumulation. Deploy De-Prescribe-Dan to unburden kidneys.
cards.gradeReason: Polypharmacy crisis + CKD + De-Prescribe-Dan as the answer — the deck closes on its most actionable clinical loop.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: toxic overload card. Subject: raccoon kidney drowning in 15 pill bottles, De-Prescribe-Dan raccoon cutting the cascade. Mood: clinical purge.

verdict: Silver Circuit is the strongest MedKayfab entry yet — every villain has a matching hero, the quest cards close genuine clinical loops, and the lore for Pallia-the-Peacekeeper will be cited in teaching rounds. Named weakness: rule-principle cards (Start-Low, Go-Slow) and screening-tool cards (Barthel, MMSE, ISAR) lose the performative edge that makes villain cards immediate. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 56 geriatric medicine cards — frailty to end-of-life — where every villain has a hero and every scenario is a real ward call. For medical students, junior doctors, and anyone who treats the 80+ crowd.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — FrizzleBob in vintage wrestling poster style, geriatric tools visible, strong composition
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — The Silver Circuit is the best deck subtitle in the MedKayfab series
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Wrestling meets geriatrics is the deck founding paradox and the cover sells it immediately
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — Silver Circuit framing for elderly patients is original and respectful simultaneously
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — High shareability in medical education community; less so outside it
coverQA.coverNote: One of the strongest covers in the corpus. The Stay Feisty! tagline and Silver Warriors closing slogan create a genuinely affectionate frame around a difficult specialty. Georg found the right tone: clinical precision without condescension.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 13 standard card pages (4 cards each = 52 cards) + 1 quest page (4 scenario cards). All text renders as embedded image — no extractable text layer. No RAF dice boxes present. The 4 quest cards on page 15 are a unique structural innovation not seen in previous decks — they function as clinical scenario integrators, linking named villain/hero cards into real ward situations. Font and artwork consistent throughout. Deck is part of MedKayfab MegaPack subfolder.
